words.desc: A reaction of the immune system to something that is normally harmless.
An emergency vehicle that rushes sick or injured people to hospital.
The joint that connects the foot to the leg.
A long-term condition in which the airways narrow and make breathing hard.
A strip of cloth wrapped around a wound or injured body part to protect it.
The small hollow or knot on the tummy left where a baby was once connected to its mother.
A small bubble of fluid under the skin, usually caused by rubbing or burning.
The red liquid that flows through the body carrying oxygen and nutrients.
A hard white piece of tissue that forms part of the body's inner framework.
The organ inside the head that controls thought, memory, movement and the senses.
The air taken into the lungs and pushed out again.
An injury in which one of the hard parts of the skeleton cracks or snaps.
A dark mark on the skin caused by blood leaking underneath after a knock.
A hard protective shell molded around a limb to hold a broken bone still.
A routine visit to a doctor to make sure you are in good health.
A mild, common infection of the nose and throat caused by a virus.
A sudden noisy push of air out of the lungs to clear the throat.
A sudden painful tightening of a muscle that you cannot control.
A pair of tall supports placed under the arms to help an injured person get around.
A series of images and feelings that the mind creates while asleep.
Either of the two organs on the sides of the head used for hearing.
The joint in the middle of the arm where it bends.
The organ of sight that takes in light so we can see.
The curved line of short hairs above each eye.
One of the short curved hairs growing along the rim of the eye.
A body temperature higher than normal, usually a sign of illness.
The hard thin plate that covers the top of each fingertip.
A viral illness that spreads easily and causes high temperature and aches.
The body part at the end of the leg that we stand and walk on.
A small light-brown dot on the skin that often appears after sun exposure.
Thin strands that grow out of the head and many other parts of the body.
The part of the body at the end of each arm used for gripping and holding.
A pain felt in the head, often throbbing or pressing.
A hollow muscular organ in the chest that keeps blood moving around the body.
The rounded back part of the foot that touches the ground first when walking.
A sudden involuntary catch of breath that makes a sharp little sound.
One of two bean-shaped organs that filter waste from the blood to make urine.
The joint in the middle of the leg that lets it bend.
A large organ in the upper right belly that cleans the blood and makes bile.
A pair of spongy organs in the chest that bring oxygen into the body.
A container of basic supplies for treating minor injuries and illnesses at home.
The opening in the face used for eating, speaking and breathing.
Body tissue that can tighten and relax to produce movement.
The narrow part of the body that connects the head to the torso.
A fiber that carries electrical signals between the brain and other parts of the body.
The part of the face used for smelling and for breathing air in and out.
A small solid dose of medicine that is swallowed whole.
A small red swollen spot on the skin, often with a white top.
The rhythmic throb felt at the wrist or neck as the heart pumps.
An area of red, irritated and often itchy spots on the skin.
The watery fluid in the mouth that keeps it moist and helps break down food.
A patch of tougher skin that remains where a wound has healed.
The rounded joint where the arm meets the upper part of the body.
The whole internal framework of bones that supports and protects the body.
The soft outer layer that covers and protects the whole body.
The bony case of the head that encloses and protects the brain.
A natural state of rest in which the eyes close and the mind switches off.
A sudden burst of air forced out through the nose and mouth.
The column of linked bones running down the back that shields a major nerve bundle.
An injury caused by twisting a joint and stretching or tearing its ligaments.
A medical instrument doctors use to listen to the heart and lungs.
Loops of thread sewn through a deep cut to hold it closed while it heals.
A stretchy bag-like organ where swallowed food is mixed with acid and broken down.
Red, sore and painful skin caused by spending too long in strong sunlight.
Medical treatment in which a doctor cuts into the body to repair or remove something.
Salty liquid that seeps from the skin when the body gets hot.
A tube with a plunger and a needle used to inject or draw out fluids.
Salty droplets that run down the cheeks when someone weeps or is upset.
The hard white structures in the mouth used for biting and chewing food.
An instrument that measures how hot or cold something is.
The short thick digit on the inner side of the hand that grips against the others.
The soft movable muscle in the mouth used for tasting and helping with speech.
A throbbing pain in the mouth, usually caused by decay or an infected nerve.
A medicine that trains the body's defenses to resist a particular disease.
A tube that carries blood from parts of the body back to the heart.
A natural substance the body needs in small amounts to stay healthy.
A rolling seat used by people who cannot easily stand or move on their legs.
The flexible joint where the hand joins the arm.
A picture that shows the inside of the body, especially the bones.
Opening the mouth wide and breathing in deeply, usually when tired or bored.
